title: Microeconomics and macroeconomics

match.reason: No bank point teaches the basic split between microeconomics (single markets, consumers, businesses) and macroeconomics (the whole economy); the closest cards cover macro and micro policy, macro objectives, or microeconomic reform, which are different ideas at a different depth.

draft.title: Microeconomics and macroeconomics
card: the study of single markets and the choices of individual consumers and businesses. It asks why one price changes or how one firm decides what to make.
the study of the whole economy. It looks at totals and averages, such as economic growth, the unemployment rate and the general level of prices.
The same event can be studied both ways. A rise in petrol prices can be studied for its effect on one household's choices, or on the whole economy's price level.
A good test is to ask what is being studied. One market, one buyer or one firm is micro. The economy as a whole is macro.
draft.remember: Micro looks at the parts of the economy. Macro looks at the whole economy.

a.q: Which topic would a macroeconomist most likely study?
opts: Why Australia's unemployment rate changed over a year
Why a bakery in Ballarat changed its bread prices
How one family chooses what to buy each week
Why the price of avocados rose in one local market
a.why: The unemployment rate measures jobs across the whole economy, so it is macroeconomics. The other three each focus on one business, one household or one market, which is microeconomics.
a.clue: Which topic covers the whole economy, not one buyer, seller or market?

b.q: Priya studies why Melbourne's rental market has fewer rentals available this year. Her teacher then asks how rising rents might affect the general price level across Australia. Which describes the two parts of the work?
opts: The first is microeconomics and the second is macroeconomics
The first is macroeconomics and the second is microeconomics
Both are microeconomics because they are about rents
Both are macroeconomics because they involve many people
b.why: Melbourne's rental market is a single market, so the first part is microeconomics. The general price level across Australia is a whole-economy measure, so the second part is macroeconomics. Many people being involved does not make a topic macro, since a single market can have many buyers.
b.clue: Ask what is being studied in each part: one market or the whole economy?

a.best: Why Australia's unemployment rate changed over a year

b.best: The first is microeconomics and the second is macroeconomics
